annotation_description: Fetching a basic Plains with Flooded Strand when the hand contains Thundering Falls (which enters tapped anyway), two Solitudes (white-heavy), Arena of Glory, Sacred Foundry, and Quantum Riddler. The hand needs both white and blue mana going forward. Fetching Hallowed Fountain (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) would provide both a Plains and an Island, enabling future blue mana for Quantum Riddler while still providing white for the Solitudes. A basic Plains only provides white mana and doesn't advance the blue mana plan. Alternatively, Hallowed Fountain could enter tapped on turn 1 (since there's no 1-drop to cast) saving 2 life while still being a dual land for future turns.

Evoking Solitude to remove Ragavan requires exiling the other Solitude from hand as the pitch cost, spending both copies of a premium card to remove a 1-mana creature. This is a massive resource expenditure (2-for-1 in premium cards) to answer a threat that, while dangerous, could potentially be dealt with more efficiently. The opponent also gains 2 life from Solitude's exile trigger.

Casting Phelia before combat means the opponent knows about it before declaring blockers, and more importantly, Phelia has flash so it could have been cast after combat or at end of opponent's turn. However, since there's no combat trick benefit to waiting (Phelia needs to attack to use her ability, so casting her main phase is fine for attacking next turn), the main concern is sequencing: playing a land first (Arena of Glory or Plains) before casting the spell would be better to preserve options. With Plains and Sacred Foundry untapped, they have exactly {1}{W} for Phelia, so no land drop is needed first. But they should consider whether holding up Solitude (which requires exiling a white card, not mana) might be better against Ragavan. On the other hand, Phelia on board provides a blocker against Ragavan and her flash means she could have been cast on opponent's end step instead, keeping mana open and maintaining ambiguity about what's in hand. Casting Phelia in main phase rather than at end of opponent's turn (using flash) gives away information unnecessarily.

The player could evoke Solitude by exiling the other Solitude from hand to exile Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer. Ragavan is a dangerous threat that generates card advantage and treasures on combat damage. Evoke Solitude would remove Ragavan (opponent gains 2 life), and the player gains life from Solitude's lifelink body entering (though it gets sacrificed). This also triggers Guide of Souls if... wait, there's no Guide of Souls on the battlefield. Let me re-check. The battlefield has Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd, Plains (tapped), Sacred Foundry (tapped). So evoking Solitude exiles the other Solitude from hand, Solitude enters, its ETB exiles Ragavan (opponent gains 2 life), then Solitude is sacrificed. This is a 2-for-1 against yourself (spending two Solitudes to remove one Ragavan), but Ragavan left unchecked is very dangerous. However, the player has Phelia which can attack and exile Ragavan temporarily (flickering it). Actually, Phelia's trigger exiles 'up to one other target nonland permanent' when it attacks - so Phelia could exile Ragavan on attack. But the player skipped their attack phase too. The player declined to evoke Solitude AND skipped attacking with Phelia to exile Ragavan. Phelia attacking to exile Ragavan would be extremely strong - Ragavan gets exiled, returns at end step under opponent's control but without dealing combat damage this turn, and Phelia doesn't get the +1/+1 counter since it returns under the opponent's control. Actually wait - Phelia's trigger says 'if it entered under your control, put a +1/+1 counter on Phelia' - Ragavan returns under the opponent's control so no counter. But the key point is Phelia can attack into a 2/1 Ragavan. Ragavan could block and trade... no, Phelia is 2/2 vs Ragavan 2/1 so Phelia survives. But the opponent might not block. Either way, attacking with Phelia to exile Ragavan is very strong. The decision here was declining Solitude, but the player also skipped attacking with Phelia (noted in 'After'). The evoke Solitude line spending two cards to remove Ragavan is debatable, but not attacking with Phelia to temporarily exile Ragavan is a clear mistake.

The player could evoke Solitude by exiling the other Solitude from hand to exile Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer. Ragavan is a serious threat that generates card and mana advantage every time it connects. The player had two Solitudes in hand, meaning they could evoke one by exiling the other as the alternative cost (exile a white card from hand). This would remove Ragavan at no mana cost while gaining the opponent only 2 life. Instead, the player declined both options, apparently believing they were 'uncastable traps,' when in fact Solitude's evoke cost specifically allows casting without mana by exiling a white card from hand.

The opponent is casting Galvanic Discharge targeting Guide of Souls (or possibly Phelia). The player has Solitude in hand which can be evoked by exiling a white card from hand. They have another Solitude (white card) to exile as the alternative cost. Evoking Solitude here would exile Ragavan (the opponent's only creature and a serious threat) while also gaining life from lifelink. Instead, the player declined to cast Solitude, apparently not recognizing that Evoke is an alternative casting cost that doesn't require mana. The opponent's Galvanic Discharge is on the stack likely targeting the player's creature, and the player is about to lose board presence without using their best defensive option.

Solitude has Evoke — Exile a white card from your hand. The player could cast Solitude by exiling the other Solitude (or another white card) from hand to exile either Ragavan or Guide of Souls. Guide of Souls is generating energy and threatening to pump attackers with +1/+1 and flying counters, and Ragavan is threatening card advantage and treasure tokens on combat damage. The player has two Solitudes in hand plus other white cards, making Evoke trivially available. This is not about having {3}{W}{W} — the Evoke cost is exiling a white card. The player's reasoning about needing mana is completely wrong and misses the alternate cost.

The player refused to consider casting Solitude during combat, treating the options as fake due to confused reasoning. Guide of Souls is a critical engine piece for the opponent that generates energy and enables flying counters. Evoking Solitude (exiling the other copy) to permanently remove Guide of Souls would have been a strong play, neutralizing the opponent's primary synergy engine.

Evoked Solitude by pitching the second Solitude to exile a creature (likely Guide of Souls), spending two premium cards to remove a 1/2. Phelia could exile Guide of Souls on the next attack for free, preserving both Solitudes for larger threats later in the game.

Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd is a 2/2 with a powerful attack trigger that can exile an opponent's creature (like Guide of Souls or Ragavan) temporarily, gaining a +1/+1 counter when the permanent returns under Gem25F Truth's control. Not attacking means missing both 2 damage to the opponent and the exile trigger. The opponent has Guide of Souls untapped as a potential blocker (1/2), but Phelia is a 2/2 and would win that combat. Ragavan is tapped. There's no reason not to attack here — Phelia's attack trigger targeting Guide of Souls would temporarily remove it (denying the opponent its energy/life gain triggers) and grow Phelia to a 3/3 with a +1/+1 counter. This is a significant missed opportunity for board advantage.

By casting Seasoned Pyromancer before playing Flooded Strand, the player will likely have to discard the land (Flooded Strand) as one of the two discards, resulting in only 1 Elemental token instead of 2. Playing Flooded Strand first would mean both discards are nonland cards (Ocelot Pride and Goblin Bombardment), creating 2 Elemental tokens and triggering Guide of Souls twice instead of once for extra life and energy.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: Discarding Ocelot Pride to Seasoned Pyromancer is a significant mistake. Ocelot Pride is one of the best cards in the Boros Energy/tokens archetype - it creates tokens every end step when you gain life (easy with Guide of Souls on board), has first strike and lifelink, and can snowball with the city's blessing. Goblin Bombardment is a good card but Ocelot Pride is a key engine piece that synergizes perfectly with Guide of Souls already on the battlefield. Flooded Strand is a land that could be played for a land drop. The optimal discard would be Flooded Strand + Goblin Bombardment (both nonland cards discarded create elemental tokens, but keeping the most impactful card matters more). Actually, Seasoned Pyromancer creates tokens for each nonland card discarded - so discarding two nonland cards (Ocelot Pride + Goblin Bombardment) creates two 1/1 Elemental tokens, while discarding Flooded Strand + one nonland creates only one token. However, Ocelot Pride's long-term value far exceeds a 1/1 Elemental token. The player should have discarded Flooded Strand + Goblin Bombardment, keeping Ocelot Pride to deploy as a powerful threat that synergizes with Guide of Souls.

Blocking Ragavan with Phelia results in both creatures trading (Ragavan 2/1 kills Phelia 2/2, Phelia kills Ragavan). Blocking Guide of Souls (1/2) instead would kill Guide while Phelia survives, since Guide only deals 1 damage to Phelia's 2 toughness. Phelia is a high-value creature with flash and flicker abilities, and Guide of Souls is an important engine piece for the opponent's energy/lifegain strategy.

Fetching Meticulous Archive (which enters tapped) instead of Steam Vents off Scalding Tarn. The player is at 13 life facing a board with Seasoned Pyromancer and two Elemental tokens. They have Quantum Riddler in hand costing {3}{U}{U}, needing 5 mana including double blue. With current lands (Plains, Sacred Foundry, Arena of Glory) plus this fetch, getting Steam Vents untapped (paying 2 life to go to 12) would give them 4 mana available this turn and access to both U and R. Meticulous Archive enters tapped, so it provides no mana this turn. While the surveil 1 is a small upside, having an untapped land this turn is more important given the pressure they're facing. Steam Vents would also still count as an Island for future Scalding Tarn fetches and provides the same blue mana for casting Quantum Riddler next turn. The surveil 1 is marginal compared to having mana available this turn for potential interaction.

Qwen3 Spike used Thraben Charm mode 1 to deal 8 damage to their own 1/1 Elemental Token, wasting both the spell and a Treasure Token to destroy their own creature for no benefit. Gem25F Truth has no creatures on board to target, but Thraben Charm has other modes - mode 2 could destroy an enchantment (none present) or mode 3 could exile graveyards (Gem25F Truth has Solitude, Phelia, Galvanic Discharge in graveyard which could be relevant). Alternatively, they could have simply not cast the spell at all.

Opponent has no creatures to block and Voice of Victory prevents the opponent from casting spells during Qwen3 Spike's turn. There is zero risk in attacking with all available creatures. Only attacking with Guide of Souls leaves at least 3 damage on the table (Seasoned Pyromancer 2/2 + Elemental Token 1/1) against an opponent at 13 life.

At 9 life facing a board of Voice of Victory (1/3, Mobilize 2, prevents spells during opponent's turn), Guide of Souls, Seasoned Pyromancer, and an Elemental token, the player likely chose Quantum Riddler over Wrath of the Skies. Wrath for X=3 would clear the entire opposing board (all creatures have MV ≤ 3), which is critical at 9 life. Voice of Victory is particularly dangerous as it creates extra attackers and shuts down interaction during combat. Leaving this board intact while deploying a single blocker risks being overwhelmed.

Qwen3 Spike passed with no creatures on board while opponent is at 9 life with an empty board and all lands tapped. They had access to Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard ability ({3}{R}{R}: create two 1/1 Elemental tokens) with sufficient mana (6 lands available), which would create immediate pressure. Alternatively, casting Goblin Bombardment ({1}{R}) would set up a damage engine for future turns.

Qwen3 Spike cast Goblin Bombardment with no creatures on board and no way to create creatures this turn, while having Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard ability available (3RR, exile: create two 1/1 Elemental tokens). The opponent is at 9 life with an empty board and all lands tapped. Two 1/1 tokens would apply immediate pressure, while Goblin Bombardment does literally nothing without creatures to sacrifice.

Quantum Riddler was warped in and its end-of-turn exile trigger went on the stack. Gem25F Truth had Consign to Memory in hand and untapped blue mana available to counter this triggered ability, which would have kept the 4/6 flyer permanently on the battlefield. Instead they declined to act, losing their only threat while at 7 life facing an opponent at 21.

Qwen3 Spike passed with an empty hand and no creatures on board, declining to activate Seasoned Pyromancer from the graveyard ({3}{R}{R}) which they had the mana for (6 lands producing enough). This would create two 1/1 Elemental tokens that could attack and/or be sacrificed to Goblin Bombardment for damage against an opponent at 7 life. With no other plays available and an empty hand, this was free value.

Qwen3 Spike declined to activate Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard ability ({3}{R}{R}: Create two 1/1 Elemental tokens) despite having 7 lands available, no creatures on board, no cards in hand, and a Goblin Bombardment that could sacrifice the tokens for 2 damage against an opponent at 7 life. This wastes a key resource that could provide both board presence and direct damage.

With an empty hand and empty board, Qwen3 Spike declined to activate Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard ability ({3}{R}{R}: exile from graveyard to create two 1/1 Elemental tokens) despite having sufficient mana (7 lands including multiple red sources). The opponent is at 7 life with Goblin Bombardment on the battlefield, meaning these tokens could deal 2 damage via sacrifice and/or attack next turn. With zero other threats available, this was their only way to rebuild pressure.

At 4 life with 8 lands available, the player incorrectly believed Solitude ({3}{W}{W}) was uncastable. With Plains, Sacred Foundry, Meticulous Archive, Plains, Hallowed Fountain providing white mana and other lands for generic, Solitude was absolutely castable. A 3/2 lifelink creature would provide crucial life gain and board presence at 4 life against an opponent with Goblin Bombardment.

Opponent is at 4 life with no board presence from Qwen3 Spike. Activating Seasoned Pyromancer from graveyard (3RR) creates two 1/1 Elemental tokens. With Goblin Bombardment on the battlefield, these tokens represent 2 damage from sacrificing + 2 from attacking = lethal over this turn and next, or at minimum puts massive pressure on an opponent at 4 life. Declining this with an empty hand and no creatures means doing literally nothing.

Qwen3 Spike declined to activate Seasoned Pyromancer from the graveyard when they had the mana to do so. Creating two 1/1 Elemental tokens and sacrificing them to Goblin Bombardment would deal 2 damage to Gem25F Truth (from 4 to 2 life). At 2 life, any creature top-decked next turn would be immediately lethal via attack or Bombardment sacrifice. With an empty hand and no board presence, this was essentially free damage that significantly increases lethal potential.

At 4 life with zero creatures on board against an opponent with Goblin Bombardment, the player declined to cast Quantum Riddler (a 4/6 flyer that draws a card on entry) and/or hard-cast Solitude (3/2 lifelink). The player was convinced the options were erroneous, but both would have provided critical board presence and survivability. Quantum Riddler via Warp costs just {1}{U} and provides a massive blocker plus card advantage. Additionally, Scalding Tarn in hand represents an unplayed land drop.

Opponent is at 4 life with no creatures. Qwen3 Spike has Goblin Bombardment on the battlefield and could activate Seasoned Pyromancer from the graveyard ({3}{R}{R}) to create two 1/1 Elemental tokens. These tokens represent 2 immediate damage via Goblin Bombardment sacrifice, or attack pressure next turn (potentially lethal with Bombardment as backup). Passing up this activation wastes a critical opportunity to close out the game against a nearly dead opponent.

The player dismissed casting Quantum Riddler as 'erroneous' believing it was already on the battlefield, but the board state shows no Quantum Riddler in play. With 8 lands available, they could cast Quantum Riddler ({3}{U}{U} or Warp {1}{U}) to get a 4/6 flyer that draws a card on entry. At 4 life, deploying a significant threat/blocker while drawing cards is critical. They should also play Flooded Strand before casting to maximize mana.

The player declined all actions during precombat main, but had Flooded Strand in hand as a land drop (no land played yet this turn) and could play it to have access to more mana or thin their deck. More importantly, the player is at 4 life facing a Goblin Bombardment with the opponent at 21 life - the game state is dire. The player has Solitude in hand which could be relevant if the opponent plays creatures. The 'Quantum Riddler' options likely represent Warp (alternate casting cost) which could be cast for {1}{U} - a 4/6 flyer that draws a card would be an excellent blocker and threat at this board state. The player dismissed all options as 'phantom choices' and 'a farce' when they likely had legitimate casting options available, particularly Quantum Riddler via Warp for {1}{U} with 8 lands available.

At 4 life facing Goblin Bombardment and an Elemental Token, Gem25F Truth has enough mana (8 lands) to hardcast Solitude (3WW) to exile the Elemental Token and establish a 3/2 lifelink creature. Instead, they passed priority repeatedly, failing to deploy their best stabilization tool. The lifelink on Solitude could gain back life, and removing the Elemental Token eliminates a Goblin Bombardment sacrifice target.

At 4 life facing an opponent at 20 life with Goblin Bombardment and an Elemental Token on board, Gem25F Truth declined to evoke Solitude to exile the Elemental Token. The opponent can sacrifice the token to Goblin Bombardment for 1 damage at any time, and having any creature on board with Goblin Bombardment is a threat. More importantly, Solitude would remove a body and gain lifelink value. The reasoning about 'hidden agendas' and 'tests' is nonsensical - this is a critical board state where removing threats matters. Even if evoke-Solitude requires exiling a white card (Consign to Memory is blue, Flooded Strand is not a card to exile), the player should at least have seriously evaluated the line rather than dismissing it with paranoid reasoning. However, the real issue is that Solitude from hand costs 3WW which they could cast with 8 lands, removing the Elemental Token and providing a 3/2 lifelink body - a significant defensive resource at 4 life.

At 4 life facing two 1/1 attackers with Goblin Bombardment on the opponent's board, declining to flash in Solitude is catastrophic. Taking 2 puts them to 2 life where Goblin Bombardment can kill them by sacrificing any single creature. Hard-casting Solitude (3WW available from 8 lands) would exile one token, block the other with a 3/2 lifelink (gaining life), and leave a meaningful body on board to stabilize.

At 2 life facing an attacking Elemental Token and Goblin Bombardment on the opponent's side, the player declined to hardcast Solitude (they had 8 untapped lands, enough for {3}{W}{W}) to exile the Elemental Token. The Elemental Token dealing combat damage puts them to 1 life, and then Goblin Bombardment can finish them off with any future creature. Hardcasting Solitude would exile the only creature the opponent has, removing both the combat damage threat and any Bombardment fodder.

At 2 life facing Goblin Bombardment + Elemental Token on opponent's board, Gem25F Truth passed their main phase without acting. The opponent can sacrifice the Elemental Token to Goblin Bombardment to deal 1 damage at instant speed, and any additional creature means lethal. Teferi, Time Raveler was available to -3 bounce Goblin Bombardment and draw a card, removing the immediate lethal threat.

At 2 life facing Goblin Bombardment (which converts any creature into direct damage), Gem25F Truth declined to cast Solitude during their combat step. Hard-casting Solitude (they have 8 lands, need 3WW which is available) would exile the Elemental Token (removing Bombardment ammunition), provide a 3/2 lifelink body that could attack to gain 3 life, significantly improving survival chances. At 2 life, every point of life and every creature the opponent has matters enormously with Goblin Bombardment on board.

At 2 life facing an opponent with Goblin Bombardment and an Elemental Token on board, passing the turn is almost certainly lethal. The opponent can sacrifice the Elemental Token to Goblin Bombardment to deal 1 damage, and any creature they draw or play can be sacrificed for the second point. Gem25F Truth had Solitude in hand which could exile the Elemental Token (removing a Bombardment sacrifice target) and gain life via lifelink, and Teferi, Time Raveler which could bounce Goblin Bombardment (the key threat enabling the sacrifice-for-damage kill). Playing Teferi to bounce Goblin Bombardment would remove the immediate lethal threat, and Solitude could be evoked to deal with creatures. Instead, they passed with 8 untapped lands and critical spells in hand.

Opponent is at 2 life with no blockers. Qwen3 Spike has lethal on board: attack with the 1/1 Elemental Token (1 damage) then sacrifice it to Goblin Bombardment (1 damage) for exactly 2. Casting Blood Moon first is unnecessary and gives the opponent a window to respond (they have blue mana open for potential interaction like Consign to Memory or other counterspells) before their nonbasics become Mountains.

Blood Moon is on the stack and will turn all nonbasic lands into Mountains. Gem25F Truth has 8 lands, of which only 2 are basic Plains - the other 6 (Sacred Foundry, Arena of Glory, Meticulous Archive, Thundering Falls, Steam Vents, Hallowed Fountain) will all become Mountains. This means they will lose access to white and blue mana entirely, being unable to cast Teferi, Solitude, or Consign to Memory. Consign to Memory specifically counters... wait, it counters triggered abilities or colorless spells, not enchantment spells. However, they could have evoked Solitude (exile a white card from hand) in response - but that doesn't help with Blood Moon. Actually, the real issue is they should have cracked Flooded Strand from hand... wait, Flooded Strand is in hand. They can't play it because it's not their land drop timing during stack resolution. Actually, looking more carefully: the choices offered are 'Solitude' and 'Scalding Tarn' (Scalding Tarn is in graveyard, not hand - this might be a UI artifact). But Consign to Memory is in hand and costs {U} - it counters triggered abilities or colorless spells, NOT enchantment spells like Blood Moon, so it can't counter Blood Moon. The key question is whether they should respond to Blood Moon somehow. They could evoke Solitude to exile the Elemental Token (pitching a white card), but that doesn't stop Blood Moon. Under Blood Moon, they lose all white/blue sources except 2 Plains. Actually wait - they have 2 basic Plains, so they still have some white mana. They won't have blue mana though. The player declined to act, which means Blood Moon resolves. With 2 Plains they can still cast some white spells. This may actually be reasonable since they can't counter Blood Moon with anything in hand. Let me reconsider - the decline seems fine since Consign to Memory can't counter Blood Moon (it's not a triggered ability or colorless spell).
